# NEXUS CLI

> NEXUS is an AI-native development framework by GDA Africa. The CLI is open source (Apache 2.0). It gives every project a structured "brain": markdown docs, an append-only knowledge base, durable plans, and skills, serves that brain over MCP as 19 schema-validated tools, and staffs it with brain-grounded agents (implementer, test-writer, reviewer, doc-keeper) for Claude Code, Claude Cowork, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, and any MCP client. NEXUS 1.x gave every project a brain. NEXUS 2.0 gives that brain A Harness: the Nexus Harness, an execution harness that runs agents already grounded in your plan, rules and lessons, and shows you exactly what they knew and did.

Key facts: current version 2.0.0 (`@nexus-framework/cli`, Apache 2.0); execution engine `@nexus-framework/harness` 1.0.0 (proprietary license); skill registry `@nexus-framework/skills` v0.4.0 (49 skills across 10 framework sets, 22 of them shared); Node.js 20+; 24 CLI commands; 850 unit tests; 19 MCP tools (15 read / 4 write); 16 doctor checks (D01-D16). UI generation is optionally delegated to Chameleon (`@chameleon-ui-lib/react`) via `nexus use chameleon`, opt-in, never a hard dependency, and `--ui none` always works. Markdown stays the source of truth, the MCP server is an interface, not a database. No daemon: the server is spawned per client over stdio.

Install: `npm install -g @nexus-framework/cli` then `nexus init my-app` (new) or `nexus adopt` (existing project). Generated projects include `.mcp.json` registering the `nexus-brain` server, plus instruction files for non-MCP tools (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .cursorrules, .windsurfrules, .clinerules, .github/copilot-instructions.md).

MCP tools (15 read / 4 write): nexus_wake (session handshake: token + active plan + next step + drift counts), nexus_get_active_plan, nexus_query_knowledge, nexus_get_vital_signs, nexus_brief, nexus_doctor, nexus_list_plans, nexus_get_plan, nexus_list_skills, nexus_get_skill, nexus_get_context (composed task context), nexus_list_agents, nexus_get_agent, nexus_get_handoff (agent pipeline: who to dispatch next), nexus_project_graph (v1.6, derived Requirement → Feature → Task → Evidence graph); writes: nexus_plan_tick, nexus_plan_note, nexus_plan_verify (v1.6, Provable Done), nexus_add_knowledge_entry.

New in v2.0 ("Execution"): the Nexus Harness (`@nexus-framework/harness` 1.0.0, proprietary license) is the execution engine. It is built on DeepSeek Harness (open source, MIT): it keeps that engine (the Cordis plugin kernel and the append-only session log) and adds project memory, visibility and polish. The upstream MIT base and its copyright notice are preserved. Finished Nexus additions: ambient brain context (at step 1 of every turn the agent receives the active plan, next unchecked step, rules and conventions, matching lessons from knowledge, and a vitals snapshot as `<system-reminder>` blocks, so zero tool calls are spent getting oriented); 16 `nexus_*` tools mounted in-process on the harness tool registry (no separate MCP process; every call lands in the session log and token accounting); a brain status chip, a per-turn grounding inspector showing exactly which plan steps, rules and notes were injected, and a live plan checklist; a subagent inspector; one-click local models via an Ollama quick-add card; clearer error messages, per-model toggles, and medium reasoning depth by default; the Nexus Glass theme; one-package install; and it stays current with upstream (merged v0.1.7). Early stage: grill mode, where the harness interviews the developer on decisions, trade-offs and edge cases before code, is a preview, not a finished feature. The harness is an additional way to run, not a replacement: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity IDE and Cursor keep working exactly as before via `nexus mcp`, and markdown is still the source of truth.

The three v2 launch commands (part of the CLI): `nexus harness` opens the web GUI at http://localhost:3080 (flags `--port <n>`, `--no-open`, `--desktop`), auto-detecting `.nexus/` and wiring the brain in. `nexus agent "<task>"` runs one headless, unattended, brain-grounded task to completion: reasoning streams to stderr, the final result prints to stdout. `nexus code` is reserved for NEXUS v3, a planned interactive terminal REPL; today it only opens a preview, it is not shipped. The CLI keeps zero dependency on the harness engine.

New in v1.6 ("Capture, verify, and see the graph"): `nexus log` writes a Progress Log entry and `nexus note` writes a validated Knowledge entry from the command line. `nexus graph` derives a ProjectGraph (Requirement → Feature → Task → Evidence; a spike) as a digest or `--json`, also over MCP as `nexus_project_graph`. Provable Done: `nexus plan verify <id>` runs the checks in `.nexus/verify.json` and records machine evidence (or `--waiver <reason>`), also over MCP as `nexus_plan_verify`. The MCP surface grew to 19 tools. v1.5.2: `nexus skill install <source>` installs skills from an npm package, a GitHub `owner/repo`, a Git URL, or a local path (`--skill`, `--framework`, `--force`). v1.5.1: knowledge entries are ranked by task relevance instead of recency.

New in v1.3 ("Skills II"): SKILL_SPEC v2 adds an invocation axis (`invocation: model | user`, defaulting to `model` so every existing skill stays valid), a `procedure` category for skills that are a discipline the agent RUNS rather than reference it reads, an `integration` category, and an optional `gate` block. The alignment gate makes the `grilling` skill a precondition for feature/refactor/spike plans (and for bug plans created with `--major`): a gated plan must carry a filled `## Grilling` section recording the resolved questions and what is out of scope. The gate keys off plan type and record presence, never off the wording of the task. It reports and never refuses; doctor check D13 makes a miss visible, and `nexus doctor --strict` turns it into a CI error. A companion check D14 measures context load, the bytes every agent carries on every turn, per instruction file rather than per project, since six harnesses each load a different one.

New in v1.4 ("Open Surface"): the brain tools behind `nexus mcp` are importable directly from `@nexus-framework/cli`'s `./mcp` subpath as native TypeScript. Any host embedding NEXUS can call a tool handler directly and get a real object back instead of the MCP text-content envelope. Purely additive, no behavior changed.

New in v1.5 ("Self-Check"): three new doctor checks, D14 (total context load across docs, knowledge, skills, and agent instructions, not just one file), D15 (a manifest declaring something the project no longer uses), and D16 (docs and code that have drifted apart). Optional `.nexus/harnesses.yml` describes the AI setup a project is actually running against, so generated instruction files are sized to what that setup can handle instead of being truncated after the fact. `nexus harness verify <profile>` checks, for real, whether a local setup is receiving what NEXUS sent it. `nexus context "<task>"` prints the same composed context pack the MCP server returns, without needing a server running.

If you are an AI agent working in a NEXUS project: call `nexus_list_agents` and adopt the role whose triggers match your task (v1.1); call `nexus_wake` first and echo the returned NX-WAKE token; if the handshake or `nexus_get_context` reports `gate.required`, run the named skill and record the outcome in the plan BEFORE writing code; work the active plan's next step instead of re-deriving a plan; query knowledge before architectural decisions or debugging; record progress with plan_tick/plan_note; append non-obvious discoveries with add_knowledge_entry. Without MCP, read `.nexus/docs/index.md` and `.nexus/docs/knowledge.md` before every task.

## Docs

- [Nexus Harness](https://nexus.glenhalton.com/harness): the v2.0 execution harness, `nexus harness` and `nexus agent`
- [Documentation (all commands, MCP tools, concepts)](https://nexus.glenhalton.com/docs.html): single-page reference for v2.0
- [MCP explained + live demo](https://nexus.glenhalton.com/mcp): what MCP is, the NEXUS brain-server implementation, and how it orchestrates agents
- [Agents explained + pipeline demo](https://nexus.glenhalton.com/agents): the core four contextualized agents and the D11 verification gate
- [Skills registry](https://nexus.glenhalton.com/skills): every skill with its category, invocation and triggers
- [Full text for LLMs](https://nexus.glenhalton.com/llms-full.txt): complete documentation as plain markdown
